\chapter{Worn out}
\label{ch:ar-worn-out}
\hlchaptermodality{514}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can talk about insomnia and exhaustion, and say that work wore me out, that someone yawned or dozed off.}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{أرق} (araq)}{أرق (araq)}]{\ar{أرق} (araq) — insomnia}

\label{lesson:AR-C514-araq}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to grow weak, then the Arabic for to bleed.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{أرق}}
\textbf{\ar{أرق}} — \emph{araq} — \textquotedblleft{}insomnia\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{عانى} \ar{أبي} \ar{من} \ar{الأرق} \ar{قبل} \ar{السفر}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ʿānā abī min al-araq qabla as-safar.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My father suffered from insomnia before the trip.
\end{quote}

Do not mix it up with \ar{عرق}, ʿaraq, sweat.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{أرق}} (\emph{araq}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʾ-r-q}, \textquotedblleft{}to be sleepless\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Araq is sleeplessness at night.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{araq}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{araq}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ʿānā abī min al-araq qabla as-safar.} — My father suffered from insomnia before the trip.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to grow weak, then the Arabic for to bleed, then say \emph{araq} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{أرق} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Insomnia\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{إرهاق} (irhāq)}{إرهاق (irhāq)}]{\ar{إرهاق} (irhāq) — exhaustion}

\label{lesson:AR-C514-irhaq}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to bleed, then the Arabic for insomnia.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{إرهاق}}
\textbf{\ar{إرهاق}} — \emph{irhāq} — \textquotedblleft{}exhaustion\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{نام} \ar{العامل} \ar{من} \ar{الإرهاق}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{nāma al-ʿāmil min al-irhāq.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The worker fell asleep from exhaustion.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{إرهاق}} (\emph{irhāq}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{r-h-q}, \textquotedblleft{}to come upon, to overburden\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Irhāq is the verbal noun of Form IV, to overburden.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{أرهق} (arhaqa)}{أرهق (arhaqa)}]{\ar{أرهق} (arhaqa) — to wear out}

\label{lesson:AR-C514-arhaqa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for insomnia, then the Arabic for exhaustion.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{أرهق}}
\textbf{\ar{أرهق}} — \emph{arhaqa} — \textquotedblleft{}to wear out\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{أرهقني} \ar{العمل} \ar{الطويل}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{arhaqanī al-ʿamal aṭ-ṭawīl.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The long work wore me out.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يرهق}, \emph{yurhiq}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{أرهق}} (\emph{arhaqa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{r-h-q}, \textquotedblleft{}to come upon, to overburden\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form IV: to put too heavy a load on someone.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تثاءب} (tathāʾaba)}{تثاءب (tathāʾaba)}]{\ar{تثاءب} (tathāʾaba) — to yawn}

\label{lesson:AR-C514-tathaaba}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for exhaustion, then the Arabic for to wear out.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تثاءب}}
\textbf{\ar{تثاءب}} — \emph{tathāʾaba} — \textquotedblleft{}to yawn\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تثاءب} \ar{الطالب} \ar{في} \ar{المحاضرة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tathāʾaba aṭ-ṭālib fī al-muḥāḍara.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

Present: \ar{يتثاءب}, \emph{yatathāʾab}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تثاءب}} (\emph{tathāʾaba}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{th-ʾ-b}, \textquotedblleft{}to yawn\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Form VI tathāʾaba is the usual verb.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{غفا} (ghafā)}{غفا (ghafā)}]{\ar{غفا} (ghafā) — to doze off}

\label{lesson:AR-C514-ghafa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to wear out, then the Arabic for to yawn.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{غفا}}
\textbf{\ar{غفا}} — \emph{ghafā} — \textquotedblleft{}to doze off\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{غفا} \ar{جدي} \ar{أمام} \ar{التلفاز}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ghafā jaddī amāma at-tilfāz.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My grandfather dozed off in front of the television.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يغفو}, \emph{yaghfū}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{غفا}} (\emph{ghafā}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{gh-f-w}, \textquotedblleft{}to doze, to sleep lightly\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Its last root letter w shows as alif in the past and as ū in the present.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ghafā jaddī amāma at-tilfāz.} — My grandfather dozed off in front of the television.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to wear out, then the Arabic for to yawn, then say \emph{ghafā} again
\end{itemize}
